title: ‘What kind of a fool am I?’ A re-examination of foolish sons in the book of Proverbs
abstract: In the book of Proverbs, foolishness is presented as a richly layered category that carries profound theological weight, integrating ethical failure, deficient judgement and spiritual waywardness. Within the broader matrix of Israelite wisdom literature, the portrayal of the ‘foolish son’ operates as a pedagogical construct, illustrating patterns of self-destructive behaviour and highlighting their extensive personal and communal repercussions. This study critically examines selected texts from Proverbs that portray the foolish son, analysing his character traits, behavioural patterns and social outcomes. Attention is given to the pedagogical role of parents within the covenantal framework of wisdom instruction. Parental guidance in Proverbs is presented as foundational for cultivating wisdom, moral integrity and social stability, thereby safeguarding children from corruption, illegitimate gain and self-destructive conduct. Conversely, the rejection of both parental instruction and the fear of Yahweh results in shame, poverty, moral decay and communal disruption, bringing grief not only to the individual but also to the family unit. By employing the historical-critical method, this study situates the relevant texts within their ancient Israelite socio-religious context while also exploring their theological coherence within the broader wisdom corpus. The findings indicate that foolishness in Proverbs is fundamentally rooted in the neglect of the fear of Yahweh and the deliberate refusal of formative instruction. Contribution: The study concludes that obedience to parental wisdom and reverence for God remain indispensable pathways to moral flourishing and societal well-being in both ancient and contemporary contexts.

title: مفهوم الدولة عند هيجل Hegel's Concept of the State
abstract: يهدف هذا البحث إلى توضيح مفهوم الدولة عند هيجل من خلال مناقشة أهم الأفكار التي طرحها حول هذا الموضوع من خلال مؤلفاته حول موضوع الدولة ومكوناتها. فهيجل حل ينظر إلي الدولة باعتبارها وحدة عضوية تتحدث عن نفسها حيث يرى أن الدولة كمجتمع يجسد المطلق عليها أن تحيا ككل حيوي وليس كمجتمع جزئي العناصر. فالدولة عنده هي تحقيق العقل والحرية الفردية حيث تألف منها النظام الشمولي وفقاً للدستور الذي يقره الشعب بكل إرادته وحديته، وأن قوة الدولة عنده هي استقرار المجتمع حيث جعل سلطتها أعلي من أي تجمع أو تشكيل سياسي فهي تمنح الافراد الطمأنينة والشعور بالسلام المرجو بين الدول. ولعل من أهم التساؤلات التي يجيب عليها هذا البحث هي. 1) ما هو مفهوم الدولة والتاريخ عند هيجل؟ 2) ماهي مكونات الدولة عند هيجل

title: Writing for wellbeing: community, heritage and the co-creation of literature
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to offer a novel literary approach to mental wellbeing and social inclusion, drawing on the findings of a series of co-created projects with community groups in Lancashire and Greater Manchester. It explores the value of reading together, writing together and researching together to reduce social isolation and improve mental wellbeing. Design/methodology/approach Researchers from the Centre for Literature and Community at the University of Greater Manchester developed a series of community arts projects (2019–2025) exploring literature as a shared resource. The respective projects used literary heritage and creative writing to co-create new cultural artefacts, transcending the limitations of an individualist, skills-based approach to literary activity. Findings The research found that participants connected with one another through the art of storytelling and that the activities improved social cohesion and perceived wellbeing. Originality/value The research challenges the hegemonic model of English literature, which reflects the cultural authority of the academic mainstream. It proposes that co-created literature offers a powerful antidote to the alienating effects of professional literary culture centred on individual readers, writers and scholars. It also suggests that literary activities have greater creative health benefits than has been previously recognised.

title: What shapes generalized and particularized trust worldwide? Population, inequality, migration and media in a global perspective
journal: Journal of International Economics and Management
abstract: Purpose This study examines the determinants of two different types of trust across continents by distinguishing between generalized trust (trust in most people and trust in strangers) and particularized trust (trust in family and neighbors). It aims to identify how media use (traditional vs. social media), net migration, demographic characteristics and economic factors are associated with generalized trust and particularized around the world and across different regions. Design/methodology/approach The analysis draws on a large, cross-national dataset of 441,481 individual observations from 107 countries, combining the EVS–WVS time series (1981–2023) with macroeconomic indicators from the World Bank, Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) and national statistical agencies. The study performs a comparative econometric analysis that is region-specific. As part of the methodology, we weight the data by both the GDP and the total population of the country in which each respondent resides. Findings The results reveal substantial continental differences in the determinants of generalized and particularized trust. Media consumption exhibits regionally contingent effects. Social media use is negatively associated with generalized trust, particularly in Europe and advanced economies (AEs), while traditional media positively predicts trust in developed contexts but negatively in developing regions. Net migration produces the most striking regional divergence. It is positively associated with trust in Europe and AEs, and Asia but strongly negatively associated in Latin America and LAFMENA (Latin America, Africa and the Middle East and North Africa – MENA). Originality/value This paper contributes to the literature in two ways. First, it advances a comparative framework that jointly analyzes generalized and particularized trust, revealing important divergences in their determinants. Second, by employing multiple weighting schemes and regional disaggregation, it tests the robustness of findings across different specifications and contexts, offering nuanced insights for both theory and policy.

title: Use of toenail clippings to document an anti-doping violation. Evidence after trimetazidine contamination, trimetazidine single administration and trimetazidine therapeutic treatment
Underemployment, need frustration, and the delayed amplification of meaninglessness in peripheral economies
abstract: Purpose This study develops and tests a dynamic deprivation model linking regional underemployment to emotional exhaustion through cumulative psychological need frustration and emergent meaningless work. It examines whether structural labour misallocation predicts intra-individual growth trajectories rather than static strain differences and whether motivational erosion generates nonlinear depletion over time. Design/methodology/approach A three-wave longitudinal panel of 336 employees in peripheral-region small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) was analysed using parallel-process latent growth curve modelling (a statistical technique that tracks how several variables change together over time). Latent intercepts and slopes (respectively, each person's starting level and their rate of change across the three waves) were estimated for psychological need frustration, meaningless work, and emotional exhaustion. Nonlinearity was tested via a latent basis specification, and moderated sequential mediation (a chain of indirect effects whose strength depends on the level of a moderating variable) was assessed using bias-corrected bootstrapping of conditional indirect effects (a resampling procedure used to test whether an indirect effect is statistically reliable). Findings Regional underemployment predicted both the level and growth of psychological need frustration, which sequentially transmitted to growth in meaningless work and accelerated emotional exhaustion. Slope-mediated pathways accounted for substantially greater variance than intercept effects. Perceived organisational support attenuated this growth-based transmission. Originality/value The study advances state-of-the-art theory by repositioning meaningless work from a contemporaneous perceptual state to a cumulative, slope-driven deprivation process rooted in regional labour structures. It integrates macro-level economic misallocation into Self-Determination Theory, identifies psychological need frustration growth as the core transmission mechanism, and empirically demonstrates delayed amplification dynamics that conventional cross-sectional mediation models cannot detect.

title: Turning familiness into firm performance: non-family employees' justice perceptions as the missing link
abstract: Purpose Family firms with comparable resources often diverge sharply in performance, yet the reasons remain unclear. This study examines how three components of perceived familiness – organizational decision-making, family culture and family image – transform into perceived firm performance via non-family employees' perceptions of distributive and interactional justice. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 400 white-collar employees in family businesses in Türkiye were used to test a model integrating the resource-based view and social exchange theory. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) assessed both the measurement model and the direct and indirect (mediating) structural effects. Findings Family culture and family image were strong antecedents of both distributive and interactional justice, whereas organizational decision-making had no significant effect on either. Both justice dimensions substantially enhanced perceived firm performance, with distributive justice being the more powerful. Mediation analyses confirmed that culture and image reach performance only through justice, whereas decision-making does not – thereby establishing organizational justice as the mechanism that converts the cultural and image components of familiness into firm-level outcomes. Originality/value Integrating the resource-based view with social exchange theory, the study shows that family resources are not inherently performance-generating; their value is realized only when employees decode them as fairness. It disaggregates familiness into components that reach performance through different routes, repositions justice from a micro-level attitude to a meso-level mechanism and reconciles the long-standing tension between socioemotional wealth and agency-based accounts of the family effect.

title: The world of information
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings This paper identified that digital business strategies help to facilitate business performance and improve innovation outcomes. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

title: The effect of board capital diversity on innovation performance: evidence from new product announcements
abstract: Drawing on the board capital perspective, this study examines how two distinct board resources – knowledge diversity embedded in directors' functional expertise and information diversity derived from their external industry ties – affect market reactions to new product introduction (NPI) announcements, and whether these effects vary with product newness and firm size. Using an event-study methodology, this study analyzes 395 NPI announcements by US-listed high-tech firms. Innovation performance is measured through cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) surrounding announcement dates. Board knowledge diversity is operationalized using Blau's index based on directors' functional backgrounds, while board information diversity is captured through industry embeddedness derived from directors' external board ties. Cross-sectional regression analyses test direct and moderating effects, incorporating product newness and firm size as contextual moderators. Board knowledge diversity is positively and significantly associated with market reactions to NPI announcements, with stronger effects for highly novel products and smaller firms. By contrast, board information diversity is negatively associated with market reactions to NPI announcements, but the association is statistically insignificant. The results are robust across alternative model specifications and measurement approaches, suggesting that internally embedded expertise plays a more critical role than external network ties in innovation governance. Moving beyond composite diversity measures, this study distinguishes the innovation-governance roles of directors' human and social capital. It further advances the literature by assessing the market-perceived value of specific NPIs and identifying product newness and firm size as boundary conditions shaping the contribution of board capital to innovation governance.
